historical_growth.owner_fcf_series_note: Owner FCF (reported FCF less SBC), FY2016-FY2025: 376, 809, 1,489, 1,309, 4,011, 2,333, 3,024, 4,919, 2,055, -135. CAGRs ending FY2025 are undefined (negative end value); the series is dominated by land-inventory swings (FY2020 and FY2023 are land run-offs, FY2025-26 a spec-home build), so no FCF CAGR is a usable growth anchor. Cumulative FY2019-FY2025 OCF 19.3bn against 23.5bn net income (~82% conversion through a full cycle including the Millrose land distribution).
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: base-path 10-year average (long-run US household formation plus nominal pricing). Equity CAGRs are not usable: the Feb-2025 Millrose spin-off distributed ~5.5bn of book value and ~8bn of buybacks since FY2021 shrink equity independently of returns; revenue CAGRs are distorted by the FY2018 CalAtlantic merger (10yr) and the FY2021-22 price peak (3yr/5yr).
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 4.1% vs revenue 5yr 8.7% and EPS 5yr 0.3% -- divergence >30% in both directions, caused by the Millrose distribution and buybacks (equity) and by the FY2022 margin peak unwinding (EPS). None of the three is used as the forward anchor.

scenario_narratives.base: Lennar's axes are (1) the mortgage-rate path and what it does to affordability-driven incentives, which at ~12% of ASP are the whole gap between today's 15.8% gross margin and a normal 20-22%; (2) the land-light trade -- lower, steadier margins and far lower capital, with Millrose and other land bankers paid through cost of sales; (3) the volume-first strategy, which protects cost per square foot and cycle time but sets price. Base: FY2027 is another soft year as the backlog and ASP reset, then rates ease and the structural shortage (household formation against a decade of under-building) lifts volume 4-5% a year. Margin recovers to a 10% land-light mid-cycle by FY2031 and holds; the terminal is capped at 13x owner FCF, a cyclical's multiple, not a compounder's.
scenario_narratives.bull: Rate relief arrives in 2027. Incentives fall to ~5%, gross margin returns to 20%+ and SG&A re-levers below 8% as Lennar grows deliveries 6-7% for three years on the same community count; EBITDA margin reaches 12%, the FY2019-FY2020 structure, on a larger and less capital-intensive base. Buybacks continue at ~1.5-2bn a year from positive owner FCF.
scenario_narratives.bear: Inflation keeps the 30-year rate near 7% through 2027-28 and consumer confidence keeps sliding (the Q3 release says conditions 'deteriorated since our last earnings call'). Lennar holds volume by cutting price another 8%, incentives rise further, margin troughs near 5.5% and inventory of completed homes needs discounting. Recovery is slow and stalls at 8% EBITDA because option premiums are a permanent cost and the asset-light structure caps margin. The balance sheet survives comfortably (net homebuilding debt to capital 12.7%), so the bear is an earnings trough, not solvency.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value the land-light homebuilder on mid-cycle owner FCF, not on the FY2026 trough and not on the FY2021-22 peak. The trough is explicit in FY0 (6.3% EBITDA, negative trailing owner FCF from a spec-home build) and each scenario is a different recovery path, so cyclicality is priced once, in the flows, with a single 10% WACC and a 13x terminal cap. Segments whose earnings are noise (Multifamily, LENx marks) are excluded from the flows and carried at book in the bridge; the mortgage warehouse is excluded from debt with its matching loans. The number to act on is the probability-weighted value; the 15% hurdle entry price is what a buyer should pay to be compensated for a cyclical whose next two years are the uncertain ones.
key_risks_to_valuation: Mortgage rates: every 1pp on the 30-year moves affordability-driven incentives by several points of gross margin; the bear case is a rate path, not a company-specific failure.
Mid-cycle margin assumption (10% EBITDA): the land-light model has no full-cycle history. If option-premium land cost plus volume-first pricing cap EBITDA nearer 8%, the base value is ~bear.

Working-capital assumption (-25% capture): a volume-first builder holding completed inventory can consume cash through a downturn rather than release it; 9M FY2026 OCF was -718 against +827 net earnings.
Terminal multiple: 13x owner FCF is above where homebuilders trade at cyclical peaks; the cap binds in every scenario, so the terminal value is a multiple judgment rather than a growth one.
Lennar Other / Multifamily carried at book (1.34bn net, ~$5.6/share): LENx public stakes are marked to market and have lost 62 in nine months; a further halving removes ~$1.50/share.
Share count: continued ~1-2bn/yr buybacks below intrinsic value are value-accretive and NOT in the model (flat count); conversely, buying back at the 2025 average of $113 was not.

inputs.base_revenue_note: FY2026E (year ending 30-Nov-2026): 9M actual total revenues 22,605.5 (Q3 FY2026 8-K ex-99.1, 2026-09-16) plus Q4 built from guidance midpoints -- 22,500 deliveries x $375k ASP = 8,437.5 home sales, plus ~230 Financial Services, ~40 Multifamily, ~22 Lennar Other and ~28 land/other. FY2025 actual was 34,186.9, so FY0 is an -8.3% year and a cyclical trough, not a run-rate.
inputs.share_count_basis: Q3 FY2026 weighted-average shares, basic = diluted (Lennar's restricted-stock awards are already in the basic count; the release reports one figure). Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows. The 31-Aug-2026 period-end count is ~1.3m lower after the 3.0m Q3 repurchase (~+0.5% to per-share values, ignored). Class A + B issued 299.7m less treasury.
inputs.net_debt_note: Homebuilding basis, exactly as the company's own 'net homebuilding debt' supplemental table: senior notes and other debts payable 4,297.3 (includes 650 drawn on the 3.1bn revolver after redeeming the 400 5.25% notes due Jun-2026) less homebuilding cash 1,150.1; restricted cash 34.1 excluded. Financial Services liabilities of 1,720.6 (mortgage warehouse lines) are EXCLUDED: they fund 2,770.7 of loans held-for-sale and are self-liquidating, and the FS segment's earnings are inside the flows, so its net assets stay as operating capital rather than in the bridge. Net homebuilding debt was only 643.4 at 30-Nov-2025; the 2.5bn swing in nine months is 1,850 of finished-home/WIP inventory build, 737+256 of buybacks and 370 of dividends against 827 of net earnings.
inputs.last_fcf_note: TTM to 31-May-2026 (latest filed cash-flow statement; the Q3 10-Q was not on EDGAR at valuation date): OCF 883.0 = FY2025 216.8 - H1-2025 (-1,384.1) + H1-2026 (-717.9); capex 166.1 = 188.6 - 71.3 + 48.8; reported FCF 716.9; SBC 139.2 = 163.5 - 112.9 + 88.6; owner FCF 577.7. FY2025 on the same basis was 28.2 reported / -135.3 owner. Both years are depressed by a counter-cyclical inventory build (finished homes and CIP 10,670 at Aug-26 vs 8,822 at Nov-25) as Lennar builds spec homes to hold volume; the projection does not carry that drain forward, which is why year-1 owner FCF (~4.9% of revenue) sits well above the trailing 1.8%.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash-flow statement ShareBasedCompensation add-back (XBRL companyfacts, filed 2026-01-28); no separate equity-award tax withholding line is tagged, and Lennar's awards are restricted stock without a disclosed net-settlement cash figure, so the add-back is used alone. FY2026 run-rate ~130 (H1 88.6), ~0.42% of revenue.
inputs.interest_income_note: Not stripped: the company is net-debt on the homebuilding basis (3,147 net debt), so the interest earned on the 1.15bn cash pile is left inside homebuilding other income and no cash is being counted twice.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 financing-activity repurchases 1,808.4 (10-K); 9M FY2026 ~993 (737 H1 + 256 Q3 at $85.49 avg). Lennar is a heavy repurchaser (~8bn since FY2021), so the flat count is funded, not a convention. Buybacks are value-neutral in this model: SBC is expensed in the flows.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate build. Risk-free ~4.3% (10y UST, Sept-2026, with mortgage rates ~6.8% per the Q3 release), ERP 5.0%, homebuilder beta ~1.35 -> cost of equity ~11.1%; pre-tax cost of debt ~5.5% on the senior notes/revolver, ~4.1% after tax; weights ~82% equity (237.8m x price ~19.5bn) / 18% debt (4.3bn) -> 9.8%, rounded to 10.0%. Same WACC in all three scenarios: cyclicality is charged in the flows via scenario paths and weights, not a second time in the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP ASC 842: office and equipment operating leases are expensed within SG&A and already inside OCF; lease liabilities are immaterial relative to a 4.3bn debt stack and are excluded from net debt. No separate lease charge (lease_cost_pct_path omitted).
inputs.nci_treatment: Charged once, in the bridge: noncontrolling interests of 137.5 (31-Aug-2026) deducted. Flows are built on consolidated revenue, but NCI took only 8.9 of 827.0 nine-month net earnings (~1%), so consolidated and attributable flows are within rounding.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (operating company, cyclical -> owner-fcf.md + owner-fcf-adaptations.md), mid-cycle normalisation of a trough year. Lennar is the largest-volume US homebuilder, land-light since the Feb-2025 Millrose Properties spin-off (owns <2.5% of its ~488,000 controlled homesites; land flows through option deposits of 7.3bn and option premiums in cost of sales). The engine's EBITDA is consolidated: homebuilding gross margin less SG&A, plus Financial Services operating earnings (mortgage/title for Lennar's own buyers -- an operating segment, already net of warehouse interest), less corporate G&A and the charitable contribution, before capitalised-interest-in-COGS and D&A. FY2026E EBITDA ~1,970 / 6.3% (9M EBIT 1,250 + D&A ~102, plus a guided Q4 at ~7%) is a trough: incentives are ~12% of ASP against a normal ~5-6%, gross margin 15.8% against 20-23% in FY2019-FY2024 and 27.5% at the FY2022 peak. Peak is NOT the anchor. Pre-COVID (FY2015-FY2019) consolidated EBITDA margins ran ~10-12% with owned land; the land-light model trades ~1-2pp of margin for lower capital intensity, so mid-cycle is taken as ~10% (base), 12% (bull: pre-COVID structure restored through scale and the 14% construction-cost reduction since Q4-2023), 8% (bear: incentives stay elevated through a long affordability recession). Multifamily and Lennar Other (LENx technology stakes marked to market, -62 in 9M FY2026) are OUTSIDE the flows and enter the bridge at book net assets. Working capital: inventory-heavy, so capture is NEGATIVE (-25% of the revenue change; owned inventory 11.5bn + deposits 7.3bn less payables 1.8bn is ~55% of revenue, but the land-light model finances most of the growth through option deposits, so a quarter of each incremental dollar is modelled as consumed). Cash tax 25.5% (FY2026 Q3 ETR 26.4%, including state tax and non-deductible compensation; Lennar is a full cash taxpayer -- FY2025 cash taxes 988.5). Terminal cap 13x owner FCF for a cyclical (the WACC Gordon at g=2.5% is 14.6x, so the cap binds in every scenario). Analysis.json was not yet available at build time; bull/bear axes are drawn from the Q3 FY2026 release and the cycle data.

bear.rationale: A two-year affordability recession: mortgage rates stay near 7%, Lennar keeps its volume-first strategy by cutting price (revenue -8% then -4%), incentives rise above 13% and margin falls to ~5.5% before a slow recovery that stalls at 8% because the land-light option-premium cost is permanent and competitors match on price. Not a 2008-style balance-sheet event -- owned land is <2.5% of homesites, so losses would hit 7.3bn of option deposits rather than a land book -- but a long, flat earnings trough.

base.rationale: FY2027 flat-to-down (Q3 orders -9%, backlog dollars -5%, ASP falling ~3%, management holding volume), then a four-year recovery at 4-5% as mortgage rates ease and the structural housing shortage reasserts, fading to 2.5% nominal. EBITDA margin climbs ~0.8pp a year from the 6.3% FY2026 trough to a 10% land-light mid-cycle by FY2031 as incentives normalise from ~12% to ~6% of ASP and SG&A re-levers from ~9% to ~7.5%; it never revisits the FY2021-22 peak (18%+).

bull.rationale: Rates fall through 2027, the even-flow machine (4.1 starts/community/month, 116-day cycle time, construction cost -14% since Q4-2023) converts into volume growth of 6-7% for three years, incentives drop toward 5% and the pre-COVID 12% EBITDA structure is restored on a larger base despite the land-light margin give-up.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 13x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: House default 15/50/35 moved to 25/50/25. Bear up to 25% because the cycle is still deteriorating at the valuation date -- the Q3 FY2026 release cut full-year deliveries, orders fell 9%, rates rose through the quarter and management says the environment worsened; a cyclical mid-way down a leg has a fatter left tail than a steady-state business. Bull down to 25% because it needs two independent things -- a rate decline AND incentives normalising without volume loss -- and Lennar's volume-first strategy means it would rather give price than margin. Balance-sheet risk is low (land-light, 16.6% debt to capital), which is why bear is 25% and not 35%.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
